root_cause.text: On UP kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, so an NMI handler can re-enter rmqueue() and acquire a zone lock already held by the interrupted context, corrupting the freelists.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held. As a result, alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter rmqueue() and acquire the zone lock that the interrupted context is already holding, corrupting the freelists." The patch adds a check to return NULL early when not SMP and in NMI.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to return NULL in the page allocator when called from NMI on uniprocessor systems, because spin_trylock always succeeds on UP and cannot protect against reentrancy.
intent_record.what: Added a condition that returns NULL if CONFIG_SMP is disabled and the current context is in NMI, before the pcp_allowed_order check.
intent_record.how: On uniprocessor systems, spin_trylock always succeeds even if the lock is held, making it unreliable for synchronization in NMI context. This guard prevents potential corruption by rejecting allocations from NMI on UP systems.
